inspection_summary: Inspected all 6,915 Python-split lines of this 154-page lecture monograph. The source develops the complex-analytic and transform machinery for zeta from maximum principles, entire functions, Gamma and general Dirichlet series through three functional-equation routes, zero distribution, Hardy's theorem, Hamburger's converse, and the Wiener-Ikehara proof of the prime number theorem. Prose is generally coherent, but many displayed formulas are fragmented by the PDF text layer; units below retain only mechanisms recoverable from the checked prose and mark formula or diagram dependence for scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, preface, and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identification, stated scope, and navigation; no depth unit.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 1: The Maximum Principle
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Maximum-modulus mechanisms, boundary formulations, minimum principles, and boundary values.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 2: The Phragmen-Lindelof principle
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Extension of maximum principles to unbounded strips via damping and interpolation.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 3: Schwarz's Lemma
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Disk contractions, half-plane transforms, coefficient bounds, and derivative inequalities.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 4: Entire Functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Weierstrass products, finite order, zero density, exponent of convergence, and genus.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 5: Entire Functions (continued)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Hadamard factorization and the relation between order, polynomial factor, and zero exponent.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 6: The Gamma Function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Mellin definition, continuation, reflection, reciprocal product, and logarithmic derivatives.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 7: The Gamma Function (continued)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Log-convex uniqueness, multiplication formula, and uniform complex Stirling asymptotics.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 8: Elementary properties of zeta
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Euler product, prime connection, logarithmic derivatives, and multiplicative coefficient identities.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 9: Elementary Dirichlet-series theory
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Partial summation, half-planes of convergence, uniqueness, and abscissae.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 10: Dirichlet series continued
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Perron inversion and two analytic justifications of coefficient-sum recovery.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 11: Continuation and functional equations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contour and fractional-part continuations of zeta and two proofs of its functional equation.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 12: Estimates and theta method
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Vertical bounds, Poisson summation, theta reciprocity, and the third functional-equation proof.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 13: Zeros of zeta
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Completed zeta, critical-strip symmetry, canonical product, and zero-free boundary.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 14: Riemann-von Mangoldt formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Argument-principle zero counting, local consequences, and auxiliary zero-count lemmas.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 15: Hardy's theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Fourier-transform route to infinitely many critical-line zeros.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 16: Hamburger's theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Converse characterization from paired Dirichlet series and a zeta-type functional equation.

sections_inspected.label: Lecture 17: Prime Number Theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Chebyshev reductions, Wiener-Ikehara Tauberian theorem, PNT, and equivalent formulations.

accepted_units.title: Maximum modulus from powering and Cauchy estimates
accepted_units.why_material: Raises the function to high powers so fixed contour constants disappear after taking nth roots, then repeats the device on derivatives to force constancy at an interior maximum.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the theorem, the powering proof, the derivative-vanishing equality case, and the note motivating removal of boundary restrictions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed Cauchy integrals are OCR-fragmented but the power-and-limit mechanism is recoverable from prose; verify formulas against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Local circular maximum principle globalized without a regular contour boundary
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the circle-mean equality case and propagates it through connectedness to obtain the interior strict maximum principle on an arbitrary domain, then locates maxima on the boundary of bounded domains.
accepted_units.context_note: The local lemma and the connectedness argument are inseparable setup for Theorems 2 and 3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose with recoverable circle integrals; one contour subscript is degraded and should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Boundary limsup control by compact exhaustion
accepted_units.why_material: Uses nested compact subsets and boundary-approaching maximizing points to convert sequential boundary limsup bounds into interior bounds, then derives minimum and boundary-value principles via reciprocals and exponentials.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the compact-exhaustion proof and the corollaries needed to interpret boundary maxima and minima.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose carries the mechanism; compact-set and reciprocal notation is legible in the text layer.

accepted_units.title: Bounded-strip Phragmen-Lindelof and multiplicative interpolation
accepted_units.why_material: Controls an infinite strip by multiplying by a Gaussian-type damping factor, applying the finite maximum principle, and removing the perturbation; normalization yields the three-lines geometric interpolation bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Starts with the crude bounded-strip theorem and includes its sharper restatement and equality case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponential damping exponent and linear weight are formula-sensitive but supported by surrounding prose; verify scan.

accepted_units.title: Half-strip Phragmen-Lindelof below the critical exponential growth
accepted_units.why_material: Builds a tailored exponential barrier whose decay dominates subcritical growth, and identifies a critical-growth counterexample showing why the threshold and barrier shape are natural.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes theorem, barrier construction, rectangle limit, sharpness remark, and immediate corollary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Nested exponentials are heavily layout-dependent; the prose makes the domination argument clear, but the exact growth formula needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Interpolation of polynomial and limiting boundary growth across a strip
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms unequal boundary powers by a single-valued complex power and transforms asymptotic boundary bounds by an auxiliary rational factor, producing interior exponents as linear interpolants.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines Corollary 2, Theorem 3, and its limiting corollaries because they share the same strip-interpolation move.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Branch and power notation is partly fragmented; mathematical prose is sufficient for planning, with scan verification required for exact exponents.

accepted_units.title: Schwarz contraction and rigidity
accepted_units.why_material: Divides out the forced zero, applies the maximum principle on expanding circles, and obtains both contraction and the rigid rotation equality case, including scaling to a general disk.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the unit-disk theorem and its scaled version.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core formulas are readable; one zero is rendered as the letter o but the context is unambiguous.

accepted_units.title: Caratheodory inequality via a half-plane-to-disk transform
accepted_units.why_material: Encodes a real-part bound as a disk-valued Möbius transform, applies Schwarz's lemma, and inverts the transform to bound the original function and identify equality cases.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes centered and translated forms and the transition to sharper coefficient inequalities.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Möbius transform and bound are recoverable, though the upper-bound symbol is OCR-corrupted; verify the displayed statement.

accepted_units.title: Borel coefficient bounds by root-of-unity filtering
accepted_units.why_material: First controls the linear coefficient from a real-part bound, then averages rotations to isolate any chosen coefficient, a reusable symmetry-projection technique.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes derivative and polynomial-growth consequences because they expose what the coefficient bound enables.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Root-of-unity cases are text-layer degraded but the averaging identity and conclusion are recoverable; scan-check indices.

accepted_units.title: One positive-real-part integral yields coefficient, increment, and derivative bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Reverses the preceding dependency chain: Fourier extraction of the nonnegative real part gives coefficient bounds directly, from which function and all-derivative estimates follow.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the preliminary real-part derivative formula and the general theorem with all three consequences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several integral and derivative displays are fragmented; prose and numbered conclusions recover the structure, but constants and powers need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Zero-free entire functions are exponentials
accepted_units.why_material: Integrates the entire logarithmic derivative to show a zero-free entire function is an exponential, then factors finitely many zeros before addressing infinite products.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the conceptual bridge from polynomial factorization to Weierstrass products.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Readable prose and formulas; no material representation ambiguity.

accepted_units.title: Weierstrass canonical product with adaptive primary factors
accepted_units.why_material: Cancels enough terms of each logarithm to make an infinite product converge locally uniformly, choosing fixed genus when a reciprocal-power sum converges and adaptive genus otherwise.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the full convergence split because it explains how arbitrary discrete zero sets are realized.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Product exponents and indices are OCR-fragmented; the two convergence cases are explicit in prose, while exact factors require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Finite order limits zero density
accepted_units.why_material: Defines order through maximum modulus and converts growth into a quantitative zero-count bound by dividing out enclosed zeros and applying the maximum principle.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the order characterization, theorem, proof, and big-O corollary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some radius arguments and powers are split across lines but recoverable; verify constants against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Exponent of convergence and genus of the zero set
accepted_units.why_material: Derives convergence of reciprocal powers from the zero-count estimate and positions canonical-product genus between the exponent of convergence and the entire-function order.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions, examples, and the integer/noninteger boundary cases.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Summation exponents are occasionally displaced in extraction; conceptual inequalities are clear, exact notation needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard factorization from logarithmic derivatives
accepted_units.why_material: Controls the logarithmic derivative after removing enclosed zeros, integrates it around expanding circles, and recovers an exponential polynomial times a canonical product for finite-order entire functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Borel-Caratheodory lemma, residue decomposition, limiting argument, and canonical-product reformulation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This span is highly formula-dependent and several residues/products are scrambled; prose preserves the proof architecture, but exact identities require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Order equals the maximum of exponential-polynomial degree and zero exponent
accepted_units.why_material: Bounds primary factors using an exponent arbitrarily close to the zero exponent, proving that total order is exactly the larger of the polynomial factor's degree and the zero-set exponent, with consequences for nonintegral order.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes canonical-product order and exceptional convergence cases needed for the equality statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primary-factor inequalities are OCR-fragmented; conclusions and case distinctions are prose-supported, exact bounds need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Gamma as a Mellin integral and factorial interpolation
accepted_units.why_material: Establishes convergence and analyticity of the Mellin integral and obtains the recurrence by integration by parts, explaining Gamma's interpolation role.
accepted_units.context_note: Stops before the preliminary integer asymptotic, which is represented later by the full Stirling unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral notation is recoverable despite layout fragmentation; endpoint conditions are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Beta integral and Gamma reflection formula
accepted_units.why_material: Changes variables in a double Mellin integral to derive the beta quotient, then specializes it to the half-value and the reflection identity that later drives zeta continuation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the justification for exchanging integrals and the contour-evaluated auxiliary integral.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Double-integral layout is degraded and the sine denominator has an OCR slip; exact formulas must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Hankel-contour continuation of Gamma and reciprocal entireness
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a keyed branch around the positive axis to express Gamma through an entire contour integral and cosecant, locating poles and residues and deducing that the reciprocal is entire.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes branch convention, small-circle limit, pole verification, residues, and continued reflection formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour orientation and branch phases are formula-sensitive; prose is coherent, but signs and factors require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Reciprocal Gamma as an order-one canonical product
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the contour estimate, zero exponent, and Hadamard theorem to factor reciprocal Gamma, determine Euler's constant, recover Gauss's limiting product, and obtain logarithmic convexity from the log derivative.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the factorization, normalization, approximation, and convexity chain together because each determines the next.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Products and logarithmic derivatives are fragmented in extraction; the chain is recoverable, while exact normalization needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Bohr-Mollerup-Artin characterization of Gamma
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that recurrence alone admits periodic ambiguity, while positivity, normalization, and log convexity squeeze any candidate between adjacent Gauss approximants and force uniqueness.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the necessary convexity facts and the squeeze proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The convexity inequalities are mostly readable; scan-check a few displaced inequality signs.

accepted_units.title: Gauss multiplication formula from Gamma uniqueness
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs a product of shifted Gamma factors satisfying the same recurrence and log convexity, invokes uniqueness up to scale, and determines the scale asymptotically.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the special duplication and triplication consequences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Shifted arguments and constants are layout-sensitive; the construction is prose-supported but formulas require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Uniform complex Stirling formula from a bounded periodic remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites log Gamma as a main term plus an integral of the bounded sawtooth remainder, integrates by parts, and obtains uniform sectorial asymptotics and log-derivative consequences.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the derivation from the product formula and all stated uniform corollaries.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This span contains many severely fragmented displays; the remainder method and sector are recoverable from prose, but exact main terms and errors must be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Euler product and zero-freeness for Re(s)>1
accepted_units.why_material: Justifies the prime-factor product by finite truncation and unique factorization, making the prime connection exact and proving nonvanishing in the absolute-convergence half-plane.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Dirichlet-series definition, convergence, product justification, and immediate zero-free consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core product is readable; a few subscripts are displaced but do not obscure the argument.

accepted_units.title: Prime data encoded by log zeta and its logarithmic derivative
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms the Euler product into a prime-counting integral, prime-power logarithmic series, von Mangoldt logarithmic derivative, and Möbius reciprocal series.
accepted_units.context_note: These linked formulas show several interchangeable encodings of multiplicative structure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some primes and minus signs are OCR-corrupted; definitions in prose make the coefficient meanings recoverable, exact signs need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Zeta products generate divisor and shifted-divisor coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Uses multiplication of absolutely convergent Dirichlet series and Euler factors to derive divisor-count, divisor-sum, and squared shifted-divisor identities later reused in a zero-free-line proof.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the general coefficient products and the positive-coefficient identity with conjugate shifts.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Multiple Euler-factor displays are heavily fragmented; the coefficient interpretations are stated in prose, exact parameter placement requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Partial summation and half-planes of Dirichlet-series convergence
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the summation-by-parts integral, uses it to prove angular uniform convergence, and thereby explains why convergence regions are half-planes supporting analytic termwise differentiation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the lemma, uniform convergence theorem, continuity consequence, and abscissa construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The general exponential Dirichlet-series notation is recoverable, though some angle and partial-sum displays need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Uniqueness of Dirichlet coefficients from remote zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplies by the leading exponential and lets the real part tend to infinity in a controlled angle, forcing the first coefficient to vanish and then iterating.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the essential positive-distance-from-boundary caveat.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; leading-term series is readable.

accepted_units.title: Absolute abscissa and singularity forced by nonnegative coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Separates ordinary and absolute convergence, bounds their gap for ordinary Dirichlet series, and shows positivity prevents analytic continuation through the convergence boundary by a Taylor-series contradiction.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes examples that distinguish convergence from singularity before the positivity theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Alternating-series example and Taylor expansion are mildly fragmented; theorem mechanism is prose-clear.

accepted_units.title: Perron coefficient-sum recovery via contour truncation and growth control
accepted_units.why_material: Proves the Mellin step-function kernel, controls Dirichlet partial sums uniformly, and moves a contour for the tail to rigorously recover a sharp partial sum from the generating series.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both preparatory lemmas, the theorem, proof, shifted form, and warning that the transformed tail rather than the raw tail must be estimated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour diagrams are absent and several integrals are fragmented; prose specifies contour sides and decay, but exact kernels need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Order-free alternative proof of Perron's formula
accepted_units.why_material: Avoids a global order estimate by splitting finite and tail series, applying partial summation at an intermediate line, and obtaining a tail bound that vanishes as the split moves outward.
accepted_units.context_note: Retained separately because the source explicitly contrasts the hypotheses and proof mechanism with the first route.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several contour integrals are OCR-fragmented and the diagram is missing; the finite-tail decomposition and estimates are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Hankel-contour continuation of zeta
accepted_units.why_material: Mellin-transforms the geometric series, wraps the kernel around its branch point, and expresses zeta as Gamma times an entire contour integral, exposing the pole at one and special values.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes interchange justification, branch contour, meromorphic continuation, residue, and Bernoulli-value consequences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Branch phases, contour, and Bernoulli expansion are formula-sensitive; exact expressions need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: First functional equation by summing contour residues
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the Hankel contour across the lattice of kernel poles, lets a square contour escape, and packages the result into the symmetric completed zeta and xi function.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the residue pair calculation, analytic continuation step, Gamma identities, and completed symmetry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The contour diagram is absent and phase factors are fragmented; the residue mechanism and final symmetry are clear, exact constants need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Second functional equation from the fractional-part Fourier series
accepted_units.why_material: Continues zeta using the bounded sawtooth error, repeatedly integrates its primitive to extend the domain, and inserts its Fourier series to derive the functional equation through sine Mellin transforms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes convergence justification for termwise integration and the Laurent constant at one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fourier and Mellin displays are fragmented; intervals and analytic-continuation logic are prose-supported, exact factors need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Vertical-strip bounds for zeta by optimized truncation
accepted_units.why_material: Compares zeta with a finite Dirichlet sum plus an integral remainder and chooses the truncation at the height, yielding logarithmic growth on Re(s)>=1 and polynomial bounds further left.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both estimates and the common truncation calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Powers in the error terms are displaced in extraction; the choice X=t and resulting regimes are clear, exact constants need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Poisson summation yields theta reciprocity
accepted_units.why_material: Derives Poisson summation from Fourier coefficients and Fejer summation under explicit convergence conditions, then applies it to the Gaussian to obtain the theta transformation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes verification of uniform convergence and Gaussian Fourier transform, not merely the final theta identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gaussian exponents and square-root factors are formula-sensitive; verify displays against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Theta-Mellin splitting gives continuation and symmetry in one formula
accepted_units.why_material: Mellin-transforms the theta tail, splits at one, uses theta reciprocity on the small-x piece, and obtains an entire symmetric remainder that simultaneously continues zeta and proves its functional equation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the source's third, structurally distinct functional-equation route.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral powers are fragmented but the split-transform-recombine mechanism is explicit; exact normalization needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Completed zeta symmetry localizes and classifies zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Uses xi's entireness, reflection and conjugation symmetries, Euler-product nonvanishing, Gamma poles, and an alternating-series sign argument to isolate nontrivial zeros in the critical strip and trivial zeros at negative evens.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes reality on the critical line, multiplicity comparison, and proof that xi has no real zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The completed-function formulas are readable with minor OCR slips; scan-check normalization and alternating-factor notation.

accepted_units.title: Xi growth forces infinitely many zeros and a canonical product
accepted_units.why_material: Combines Stirling and zeta bounds to identify xi's order-one but non-minimal growth, then invokes the earlier entire-function theory to force infinitely many zeros and derive product and logarithmic-derivative expansions.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the explicit payoff of Lectures 3-5 for zeta zero theory.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Canonical product and logarithmic derivative are OCR-fragmented; theorem conclusions are clear, exact factors need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Zero-freeness on Re(s)=1 from positivity
accepted_units.why_material: Gives two distinct positivity mechanisms: a nonnegative trigonometric polynomial applied to log zeta, and a positive-coefficient Dirichlet series whose convergence boundary must be singular.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains both proofs because one is local Euler-product positivity and the other reuses the general boundary-singularity theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The first inequality and shifted-product identity are formula-sensitive; prose clearly states both contradictions, exact exponents need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-von Mangoldt formula by symmetry and argument variation
accepted_units.why_material: Counts xi zeros with the argument principle, reduces the contour by completed-function symmetries, evaluates Gamma's phase with Stirling, and bounds zeta's remaining phase by counting real-part crossings.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Backlund zero-count estimate used to control the argument error and removal of the generic-height restriction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The rectangle diagram is absent and phase formulas are fragmented; contour roles and asymptotic conclusion are recoverable, exact main term needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Local zero density and asymptotics of ordered zero ordinates
accepted_units.why_material: Extracts O(log T) zeros in fixed-height windows, reciprocal-ordinate sum bounds, and gamma_n asymptotics from the global counting law.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the corollaries and convergence threshold remarks.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: A few sums have displaced primes/subscripts; meanings are stated in prose, exact estimates need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Disk zero bound and argument principle
accepted_units.why_material: Factors zeros through disk automorphisms to compare zero count with maximum modulus, then states the logarithmic-derivative argument principle used in the zero-count proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The appendix records the exact local tools invoked above.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One automorphism denominator is OCR-corrupted; scan verification is required for the exact factor, while the modulus-one argument is clear.

accepted_units.title: Hardy's Fourier-transform contradiction for infinitely many critical-line zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Represents the real critical-line xi function as a cosine transform, inverts it, and shows that eventual constant sign would force high even moments and derivatives to have one sign, contradicting boundary decay inherited from theta reciprocity.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes construction of the transform kernel, Fourier inversion conditions, moment argument, and theta-boundary decay.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several key displays and the final contradiction are text-layer fragile; the strategic chain is prose-recoverable, but exact kernels and derivatives require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Hamburger characterization from a zeta-type functional equation
accepted_units.why_material: Uses Mellin inversion to turn paired Dirichlet series and their functional equation into a theta-like transformation, shifts contours across finitely many poles, and exploits imaginary periodicity and residue equality to force constant coefficients and hence a scalar zeta function.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the transform lemmas, Phragmen-Lindelof growth control for contour shifting, residue polynomial, and periodicity conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This proof is highly formula- and contour-dependent, with many fragmented exponents; the architecture and coefficient-forcing step are explicit, exact identities need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Chebyshev functions transfer the prime number theorem among three normalizations
accepted_units.why_material: Builds the prime-counting, theta, and psi encodings, proves their upper and lower limiting behavior agrees, and connects psi to the logarithmic derivative of zeta.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes reciprocal-prime divergence as motivation and the precise limiting-indetermination comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose and recoverable sums; a few floor and prime-power indices need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Wiener-Ikehara from triangular Fourier smoothing and monotonicity
accepted_units.why_material: Subtracts the pole, smooths the boundary Fourier transform with a triangular kernel, passes to a positive convolution, and uses monotonicity to squeeze the normalized counting function to one.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both limsup and liminf arguments; they are essential to the Tauberian conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Kernel formulas and limit displays are heavily fragmented but the smoothing, positivity, and squeeze logic is explicit; exact normalizations require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Prime number theorem from zero-freeness, and zero-freeness back from PNT
accepted_units.why_material: Applies Wiener-Ikehara to the von Mangoldt transform using zeta's sole boundary pole and zero-free line, then reverses the logic by showing a PNT error transform cannot have a pole at 1+it.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both causal directions between the analytic boundary condition and psi(x) asymptotics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Transform signs are readable with minor extraction issues; scan-check the normalization by s in the logarithmic derivative.

accepted_units.title: Prime-counting asymptotics are equivalent to nth-prime asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers between a monotone counting function and its generalized inverse using logarithmic equivalence and adjacent-prime squeezing.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the source's chain from zeta boundary behavior to the magnitude of the nth prime.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: One pi symbol is OCR-rendered as tau, but the surrounding statements identify the intended counting function; verify against scan.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Maximum principles as growth-transport devices
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source progressively turns local maximum control into stripwise and asymptotic interpolation by introducing barriers whose boundary effect vanishes while their growth effect persists.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a within-source methodological relation, not a claim that all later strip estimates reduce to one identical theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Real-part control feeds entire-function factorization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Disk/half-plane transforms and coefficient estimates control logarithms of zero-removed functions, supplying the derivative bounds used in Hadamard factorization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact constants and some displayed formulas are OCR-sensitive and require scan verification before training use.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Canonical products recur from arbitrary zeros to Gamma and xi
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The monograph reuses one architecture: zero locations determine a canonical product, growth bounds restrict the residual exponential polynomial, and logarithmic differentiation converts zeros into analytic identities.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The functions have different normalizations and growth evidence; this synthesis does not identify their products term by term.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Three functional-equation routes expose complementary structure
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Contour residues expose the pole lattice, fractional-part Fourier analysis exposes periodic error, and theta-Mellin splitting exposes self-reciprocity; each reaches the same completed symmetry through a different representation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Equivalence is only at the final zeta identity; intermediate hypotheses and analytic continuations differ materially.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Dirichlet-series inversion connects analytic functions back to coefficients

within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source's sharp cutoff convention and convergence hypotheses remain essential and should not be generalized silently.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Completed zeta links symmetry, growth, products, and zero counts
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Completion converts the zeta functional equation into an entire symmetry; Stirling growth then enables canonical products and argument-principle counting, which in turn yields local zero-density information.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These results establish location symmetry and density, not the Riemann hypothesis.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Positivity at the boundary is the bridge to primes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Euler-product positivity excludes boundary zeros, positive-coefficient singularity principles diagnose forbidden continuation, and Tauberian positivity turns the surviving pole into prime-counting asymptotics.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The Tauberian conclusion also uses monotonicity and exact analytic boundary hypotheses, not positivity alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Fourier and Mellin transforms serve distinct inversion roles
